repository.name: @webex/helper-image
repository.purpose: A Webex JavaScript SDK helper package that reads EXIF orientation onto image files, resolves their MIME type, and measures and thumbnails them through separate Node and browser implementations.

commands.compile: [NEEDS HUMAN INPUT] -- no standalone compile step exists: the sources are JavaScript transpiled by Babel as part of build:src, and package.json declares no typecheck or compile-only target.

public_interfaces.name: Package export surface
public_interfaces.audience: Webex SDK plugins that prepare files for upload, plus external npm consumers
public_interfaces.notes: Verify against the declarations in src/index.js and the entry points in package.json. The package ships no .d.ts and no API report, so those two files together are the ecosystem-native declaration. The module-internal orient helper is not part of this surface, even though README.md documents it as if it were.

public_interfaces.name: Runtime substitution map
public_interfaces.audience: Bundlers resolving the package for Node or for a browser
public_interfaces.notes: The browser field decides which processImage implementation a browser consumer receives, for both the source and built paths. Treat it as contract rather than build configuration.

public_interfaces.name: Package scripts
public_interfaces.notes: Run each script through yarn workspace from the workspace root. Do not run the aggregate test script: it chains yarn test:integration, which package.json does not define, so it fails before reaching the browser tier.

generated_artifacts.refresh_with: Re-run the Repo Annotation template setup from the active plugin installation; the template snapshot is shared from the enclosing workspace and reached through the .sdd/templates symlink.

affects: The published package export surface, so every SDK plugin and external npm consumer
change_impact.notes: Renaming, removing, or reshaping an export here is a breaking change for external consumers and must land with a coordinated workspace release.

affects: Node consumers only; the browser bundle receives the other implementation
change_impact.notes: Change the browser implementation in the same edit or record deliberately why behavior now differs by runtime. Nothing in the build or test suite catches drift between the two files.

affects: Browser consumers only, including thumbnail dimensions and the EXIF orientation transform
change_impact.notes: The orientation transform table is the one behavior this package verifies exhaustively; the unit suite asserts exact transform arguments for all eight EXIF values.

affects: Which processImage implementation each consumer resolves, plus the published entry points
change_impact.notes: The browser field is part of the public contract. No test asserts the substitution, so review it by hand.

affects: The canonical specification and the standing documentation agents read first
change_impact.notes: README.md is the consumer-facing npm readme, kept separate as reference-only context. Specification changes belong in src/docs/README.md, which is the authority on the public surface. No command validates documentation directly; re-run the unit suite to confirm the behavior a specification change describes still holds, and re-read the cited source files for the parts the suite does not cover.

glossary.definition: An integer from 1 to 8 describing how a JPEG must be rotated or flipped for correct display, where 1 means no transform is needed.
glossary.notes: Mapped to canvas transforms in src/orient.js. Values outside 1 to 8 fall through the switch and apply no transform while still drawing.

glossary.definition: A caller-supplied object carrying image bytes plus loosely typed metadata; it may be a DOM File or Blob or a plain object, and this package writes orientation results back onto it.
glossary.notes: The MIME type may appear as type or as mimeType. Avatars set type while activity files set mimeType, which is why both are checked.

glossary.definition: The positional array of thumbnail, file dimensions, and thumbnail dimensions that processImage resolves to.
glossary.notes: Empty slots are undefined on Node and null in the browser, so consumers must not distinguish the two.

glossary.definition: An image treated as a profile picture, whose reported dimensions are squared to its larger side.
glossary.notes: Honored only by the browser implementation; the Node implementation does not accept the option.

evidence_rules.requirement: A command must appear in the scripts block of package.json before it is documented. Verify it is actually defined rather than only referenced: the aggregate test script references test:integration, which does not exist.
evidence_rules.notes: Document commands in their yarn workspace form, because this package builds and tests from the workspace root.

evidence_rules.requirement: A public import must be re-exported from src/index.js. A symbol reachable only by a relative path into src is internal, regardless of how README.md describes it.
evidence_rules.notes: The orient helper is the standing example: it is imported by the browser implementation and by the unit suite, and is not part of the package surface.

evidence_rules.requirement: Attribute behavior to the specific implementation file, and state which runtime it applies to whenever the claim touches processImage. Check both implementations before describing processImage behavior as a property of the package.
evidence_rules.notes: A test assertion is evidence only when it executes. The readExifData cases are disabled with xdescribe and the updateImageOrientation cases run only under the browser runner.

evidence_rules.requirement: Mark an unresolved fact explicitly rather than inferring it, and record the same status in the manifest so downstream work can see it.
evidence_rules.notes: Absence of a coverage gate for this package is a verified fact declared by the owner, not an unresolved value.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not describe processImage behavior without naming the runtime.
negative_guidance.why: Two implementations are selected at bundle time by the browser field in package.json, and they genuinely differ in type fallback, avatar handling, and the value used for empty result slots.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat README.md as a specification.
negative_guidance.why: It is the consumer-facing npm readme, retained as reference-only context. It omits processImage and detectFileType and presents the internal orient helper as a package export.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not add a runtime environment check to choose between the two implementations.
negative_guidance.why: The browser field in package.json is the selection mechanism. A runtime check would bypass it and ship both code paths into every bundle.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer that the unit suite pins current behavior.
negative_guidance.why: Only the orientation transform table is exhaustively covered. detectFileType and both processImage implementations have no tests, and the EXIF cases are disabled.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer a coverage or quality gate for this package.
negative_guidance.why: No coverage script exists here and the inherited Jest configuration disables coverage collection. The absence was confirmed by the package owner.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not assume the aggregate test script runs the suite.
negative_guidance.why: It chains yarn test:integration, which package.json does not define, so it fails before reaching the browser tier. Run the tiers individually.

high.expectation: The claim is backed by a named file in this package and, where behavior differs by runtime, by both implementation files. Proceed and cite the paths.

medium.expectation: Evidence covers one runtime, or an assertion exists but does not execute. State the runtime and the coverage limitation, and omit the part that is unproven.

low.expectation: No file in this package supports the claim. Stop and report the gap rather than deriving it from the consumer readme, from a sibling package, or from commit history.

main_entrypoints.name: Package entry
main_entrypoints.purpose: Declares the EXIF orientation functions and re-exports the MIME detection and image processing helpers as the package surface.
main_entrypoints.notes: Referenced by devMain in package.json; main points at the built output.

main_entrypoints.name: Agent entry
main_entrypoints.purpose: First document an agent reads before changing this package.
main_entrypoints.notes: Routes to the standing docs and to the module specification.

workspace_packages.name: @webex/helper-image
workspace_packages.notes: This specification root is a single workspace member of the Webex JavaScript SDK. It contains no sub-packages, and its sibling dependencies resolve through the workspace protocol declared in package.json.

source_surfaces.name: Image helpers module
source_surfaces.notes: The only module. Five flat source files behind one entry point, specified at src/docs/README.md.

source_surfaces.name: Unit suite
source_surfaces.notes: One spec file executed by both the Mocha and Karma runners, with cases gated by runner.

source_surfaces.name: Standing documentation
source_surfaces.notes: Generated documentation navigation, architecture, onboarding, decisions, and the specification registry.

source_surfaces.name: Inherited tooling configuration
source_surfaces.notes: Each re-exports a shared workspace configuration. jest.config.js is present but no script invokes Jest; the real runners are Mocha and Karma.

generated_surfaces.name: Repo Standards template snapshot
generated_surfaces.refresh_with: Re-run the Repo Annotation template setup from the active plugin installation.
generated_surfaces.notes: Reached through the .sdd/templates symlink to the shared snapshot in the enclosing workspace, so this package holds no template copy of its own.

generated_surfaces.name: Built package artifact
generated_surfaces.notes: The published artifact referenced by main in package.json. Never edit it directly.

sync_paths.mechanism: Repo Annotation template setup, resolved from the bundled snapshot in the active plugin installation.
sync_paths.notes: The snapshot is shared at the workspace level and reached by symlink, because the canonical template root must be a path inside this specification root.
Transpiles the sources through the shared legacy build tooling.

validation_entrypoints.name: Unit tests
validation_entrypoints.scope: The unit suite under the Mocha runner. Cases gated to the browser do not execute here.
validation_entrypoints.notes: The fastest signal, but it leaves part of the suite unexecuted.

validation_entrypoints.name: Unit tests in a browser
validation_entrypoints.scope: The same spec file under Karma, which is the only way the browser-gated cases run.
validation_entrypoints.notes: Requires a local Chrome and Firefox, the runner defaults.

validation_entrypoints.name: Lint
validation_entrypoints.scope: ESLint across the sources, using the inherited shared configuration.
validation_entrypoints.notes: Also the formatting check; there is no separate format command.

validation_entrypoints.name: Build
validation_entrypoints.scope: Transpiles the sources into the published artifact without running tests.
validation_entrypoints.notes: There is no standalone compile or typecheck step in this package.

rules: Orient the reader before describing detail: state what the folder owns and what it does not before naming files.
Name the runtime whenever behavior differs between the Node and browser implementations.
Cite a file in this package for every behavioral claim.
folder_readme_contract.example_policy: Include an example only when it is copied from a source or test file in this package and still matches it. Do not invent usage that no call site or test demonstrates.
folder_readme_contract.fallback: When a folder has no owned behavior beyond its parent module, omit a folder readme rather than restating the module specification.

regression_feedback_rules.trigger: A change lands in one processImage implementation and not the other, so behavior diverges by runtime.
required_followups: Require the paired file in the same review, per the change-impact rows above
Add a regression test for the changed behavior under both the Mocha and Karma runners
Record the divergence in the module specification when it is deliberate
regression_feedback_rules.notes: Nothing in the build or test suite detects this today, which is how the existing differences in type fallback, avatar handling, and empty-slot values accumulated.

regression_feedback_rules.trigger: Documentation describes the module-internal orient helper, or omits processImage and detectFileType, as the consumer readme does.
required_followups: Correct the surface against the declarations in src/index.js
Leave README.md unchanged, since it is reference-only, and fix the specification instead
regression_feedback_rules.notes: The module specification is the authority on the public surface.

regression_feedback_rules.trigger: A test is added to the disabled EXIF block without re-enabling it.
required_followups: Re-enable the block or state explicitly that the path stays unpinned
Record the remaining gap in the module specification verification table
regression_feedback_rules.notes: Assertions that do not execute are not coverage, and the EXIF path is the largest untested surface in this package.

surface_owners.edit_boundary: Owns every file under src. Changes to an export in src/index.js, or to one processImage implementation alone, are consumer-visible and need review.
README.md is retained unchanged as reference-only npm documentation. Specification corrections belong in src/docs/README.md.
Consumed as-is. This package authors no lint, Babel, Jest, or runner configuration of its own and should not fork one.
Never edit template bodies. They are shared at the workspace level and reached through the .sdd/templates symlink.

fallback_rules: When behavior cannot be attributed to a file in this package, stop and report the gap rather than deriving it from the consumer readme, a sibling package, or commit history.
When a claim holds on one runtime only, say which runtime rather than generalizing it to the package.
When a needed command is absent from package.json, ask for the exact command instead of composing one.
